newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr seen range-bound in Asia after recent moves.
newsitem.headline: Dlr seen range-bound in Asia after recent moves.

text.p: The dollar is likely to take a breather in Asia on Wednesday after wild movements over the past two days following remarks by Japanese officials warning of an excessive dollar rise, dealers said.
"Although a strong dollar trend could stay intact, the dollar is likely to move into a narrow 115-116 yen range for a while after recent fluctuations," said a trust bank dealer.

Dollar purchases by Japanese importers and some investors could give support at around 114.80 yen, while the topside is likely to be inhibited by investors' hedge sales, profit-taking and mark sales against yen by overseas operators.
The dollar fell against the yen on Tuesday in New York, partly hit by comments from Gail Fosler, chief economist at the Conference Board, a private economic research firm.
Fosler told an audience in Washington that the dollar was 15 percent overvalued against the yen, fueling a brief flurry of dollar selling, dealers said.
Dealers in Tokyo said that the dollar should be well-bid below 115 yen and further falls in Tokyo stocks could push the dollar higher to 115.50 yen and above.
A dealer at a European bank said the dollar's tospide was likely to be capped over the next few weeks.
"The dollar is likely to be stuck over the new few weeks before climbing to 118 yen on a medium-term basis," said the European bank dealer.
He said unwinding of mark/yen long positions could indirectly cap the dollar/yen's rise, with selling pressure seen emerging at 74.00 yen.
The mark was standing at around 73.76 yen in early trade against 74.00 yen in late Tokyo trade on Tuesday.
